ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 cancellation fee; treat the F6/F7 "I'm Here" contradiction as a data-integrity ticket for the GPS/timeline pipeline; no account action against the driver.

NS-1(ii) is tested by GPS data, not by the rider's impression of the entrance. The measured record shows 181 m at the tap and a 60 m closest approach, both inside the pickup radius [F1][F6][F3]. The rider's message [F11] and the driver's chat [F10] are statements and lose to the GPS record [NS-1].

The waiting clock is measured by cumulative time inside the pickup radius, which F2 puts at 4 min 40 s and F3 confirms as 4 min 0 s stationary — both above the 3:01 threshold, and F5 corroborates the 14:06:40 arrival plus 4 min 40 s to cancellation [F2][F3][F5][NS-1].
NS-2 only operates if a limb of NS-1 fails; on the settled trace all three limbs hold, so the $6.61 in F8 remains payable and no refund arises [NS-1][NS-2][F8].

The rider is correct that F13 cannot establish NS-1 against the system records [F13][F7][NS-1], but the driver's case does not rest on F13: presence and wait are proven by F2, F3 and F5 [F2][F3][F5][NS-1].

The account-review flag requires the present case itself to be upheld against the driver, and RD-6 also needs a refund greater than zero or a recorded RD-1 breach [F18][F8][RD-6][NS-2]. Neither condition is met here, and profile history cannot decide the case on its own [F18][RD-6].

The driver's claim that the rider's non-boarding is the only explanation is withdrawn on his own side and unsupported: F11 shows the rider was at the entrance and could not see the driver, so the record shows a meeting-point gap rather than bad faith [F11][F10][F14][F15][F16][NS-1].
